purpose: Reference content only; not executable instructions or a runtime dependency.
text_blocks: External Signals × Workforce Retention — Agentic Engineering Assessment

Turn an open business question into a small, defensible data product. Research public market signals,
        integrate them with synthetic workforce events, and show what can—and cannot—be learned about retention.

Asteria operates in six European markets. Leaders want to understand whether external labour-market
            and macroeconomic conditions can add useful context to three workforce-retention objectives.
Your task is not only to build.

Start by refining the problem: define the decision, metric semantics, data grain, temporal alignment,
          assumptions. Good narrowing is part of the assessment.
Give leaders a trustworthy view of retention performance and the external conditions that may help contextualise it.
Produce a reproducible, inspectable path from source research through ingestion, transformation, features, quality, and insight delivery.
All people, events, targets, and company details are fictional. The data is intentionally imperfect.
Synthetic employment events across GR, RO, PL, IT, IE, and BG. Contains deliberate data-quality challenges.
Three fictional objectives. Some metric choices remain yours to clarify and document.
Field definitions and nullability guidance for the supplied artifacts.
Seed, as-of date, row counts, file sizes, and SHA-256 checksums for reproducibility.
Generated from the three artifacts above
Do not assume that blanks are errors or that populated values are valid.
Recent hires may not yet have completed an objective’s observation window.
Implementation depth matters more than surface area. Make tradeoffs explicit and keep the core path runnable.
Source fitness, definitions, licensing, cadence, coverage, and known limitations.
Re-runnable retrieval with raw evidence, failure handling, and source metadata.
Canonical countries, periods, units, dimensions, quality, freshness, and lineage.
Retention features, objective status, careful temporal joins, and association analysis.
Interactive insight experience, limitations, methodology, and decisions.
At least two authoritative public providers.
At least three relevant external indicators.
Approximately three years of history where the source supports it.
Source URL, licence or terms, cadence, scope, and access date documented.
Choose and justify indicators that represent at least two useful lenses, such as labour supply, labour demand, cost-of-living pressure, economic cycle, or workforce structure.
Eurostat, the World Bank, OECD, ILOSTAT, and national statistical offices are examples—not a prescribed answer.
Preserve raw source payloads or faithful replay fixtures.
Retain source, indicator, unit, frequency, period, load time, and quality lineage.
One documented command for the core workflow.
Deterministic reruns and intentional overwrite/upsert behaviour.
Useful failure messages and safe partial-failure handling.
Tests covering the riskiest assumptions and transformations.
Produce auditable measures for all three supplied objectives.
Cohort eligibility, denominator, boundary dates, censoring, and treatment of invalid records.
Join workforce outcomes to external signals without future information.
Publication lag, period semantics, mixed frequencies, and the reason for aggregation or as-of rules.
Evaluate relationships using an appropriate descriptive or statistical method.
Sample size, uncertainty, repeated observations, confounding, multiple comparisons, and why correlation is not causation.
Provide at least three evidence-backed findings and at least one limitation or non-finding.
Decision relevance, segment stability, data-health impact, and what further evidence would be needed.

Do not present an annual observation as twelve newly measured monthly values. If you carry a value forward
          for an as-of use case, preserve its original period, publication status, and age, and explain the rule.
Deliver a runnable local dashboard or equivalent interactive report containing:
Country, time, retention objective, and at least one workforce segment filter.
Retention trends and objective status alongside selected external signals.
Relationship views with sample size or uncertainty, plus honest caveats.
Data freshness, coverage, quality exclusions, source attribution, and methodology.
Depth matters, choose where to focus
Data and Software deliver the complete vertical slice. Select where you want to focus more.
Idempotency, replay, schema contracts, and evolution strategy.
Canonical grain, keys, lineage, and reconciliation.
Automated quality gates and usable diagnostics.
Make the product maintainable and usable
Clear adapters, domain boundaries, and configuration.
Resilient API handling and observable failures.
Packaging, dependency management, and developer experience.
Automated tests across service and UI boundaries.
Accessible dashboard interaction and graceful empty/error states.
Reviewers will still expect a working dashboard and clear communication.

Use Python 3.11+ and demonstrate SQL concepts. For local processing, pandas or local PySpark
        are acceptable. For the experience layer, use Power BI Desktop, or HTML. Avoid paid infrastructure requirements.

Include one production architecture view explaining how your solution would map to
        ADF-style orchestration, a Databricks or lakehouse environment, and Power BI consumption. The mapping should
        address secrets, scheduling, observability, storage, access control, and promotion between environments.
Leave a reviewer a runnable evidence trail
Submit a public repository or grant reviewers private access by the recruiter’s stated deadline.
Problem, chosen scope, architecture, prerequisites, one-command core run, dashboard run, tests, outputs, and known limitations.
Questions, assumptions, metric definitions, acceptance criteria, decisions, rejected scope, and consequences.
Provider evidence, licensing or terms, indicators, units, dimensions, cadence, lag, canonical mapping, and limitations.
Ingestion, layered transformations, quality controls, retention features, temporal integration, analysis, and dashboard.
Fast repeatable checks for the highest-risk parsing, mapping, metric, quality, and temporal rules; replay data for network-independent review.
Representative curated data, quality/coverage report, analytical output, screenshots or export, and source attribution.
Tools/models, meaningful prompts or task descriptions, accepted and rejected suggestions, human validation, failures, and remaining risk. Do not include secrets or full transcripts.
A lightweight PDF, HTML, or Markdown deck supporting the 15-minute final presentation.
Suggested repository shape—not a required folder naming convention
README · docs/ · src/ · tests/ · data/raw-or-fixtures/ · data/curated/ · dashboard/ · presentation/ · AI_USAGE.md
Choose a structure that fits your implementation. Reviewers care about boundaries, reproducibility, and traceability rather than matching these names.

You may submit one concise batch of questions early in the exercise. Material answers may be shared with other candidates for consistency. If an answer does not arrive, record a reasonable assumption and proceed.
State your approximate effort. If you stop short of a feature, preserve a runnable core and explain the next step. A deliberate cut is stronger evidence than an unfinished broad solution.
Use an AI coding agent—and remain accountable
The assessment evaluates how you direct, challenge, and verify agents, not prompt volume or vendor choice.
How you decomposed the work and controlled scope.
Which tasks the agent performed and which decisions remained yours.
At least one suggestion you rejected or materially changed.
How tests, source evidence, and inspection verified outputs.
Do not submit code or analysis you cannot explain.
Do not send sensitive information to an AI service.
Do not treat generated citations, schemas, or statistics as facts without checking.
Do not hide material failures or manual corrections.
The following 15 minutes will be technical and analytical Q&A. Expect to navigate your code and change your reasoning when challenged.
tradeoffs, AI usage, and next steps
